title: Montclair Retail  integration call notes (2026-03-30)
content:
Attendees: Montclair Retail (Sara Park - Head of ML, Omar Ruiz - Platform Eng, Jenna Li - Security); Redwood: Matthew Chen (SE), Priya Nair (Customer Success), Luis Gomez (Solutions Eng)

Purpose: initial integration sync to capture requirements, constraints, and next steps for productionizing Redwood inference on Montclair's platform. Customer is evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for checkout recommendation and search re-ranking use cases.

Customer background (quick):
- Retail chain with ~1,200 stores + e-commerce site. Sensitive PII in order history; model inputs may include partial customer data (hashed IDs, purchase items).
- Platform: primarily GCP, some on-prem legacy infra for POS analytics. Considering hybrid: Dedicated in Redwood-hosted region + VPC for sensitive workloads.

Key requirements / asks:
1) Data residency & isolation: must ensure no customer data leaves their VPC for certain workloads. Looking at Private deployment with customer-managed control plane; explained difference between Dedicated (isolated capacity but control plane managed by Redwood) vs Private (customer control plane + VPC peering / on-prem).
2) Latency SLOs: 95th perc tail < 120ms for short re-rank (seq len ~64), batch scoring up to 50 QPS during peak. Checkout completions (longer context ~512) can tolerate up to 500ms p95.
3) Throughput: expected baseline 10-15 QPS for re-rank, spike up to 50 QPS Black Friday planning. Embeddings workload: nightly bulk (50k requests) and near-real-time vector lookups (~40 qps).
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 + PCI-sensitive flow around payment tokens. KMS/HSM integration mandatory for tokenization keys. Audit logs must be retained 90 days and exportable to their SIEM (Splunk).
5) Model choice & quality: prefer open-model baseline (Llama2-13B or Mistral-equivalent) for cost control but want Redwood to run an eval against existing on-prem model for parity. Concern about hallucination on product attributes - ask for guardrails and structured outputs.
6) Rollout: canary 5% traffic, A/B test against current on-prem model, automatic fallback to smaller model when latency breach/overload detected.

Gotchas / Risks called out during call:
- Prefix caching: their UI app often concatenates user history + product catalog snippets. Need to ensure caching keys align with user privacy (personalization can't be cached globally). Suggested solution: per-user KV cache encryption or rely on Dynamic Context with server-side cache only for anonymous prefixes.
- Tokenization mismatch: their infra currently uses an in-house tokenizer for product SKUs; need to validate tokenizer compatibility with chosen model. Action: run tokenization diff job.
- PCI scope: while model inputs don't include raw card numbers, their telemetry pipeline sometimes samples events that contain masked card fragments - must ensure ingestion pipelines filter out remaining sensitive snippets before sending to Redwood endpoints.
- Network egress constraints: their security team is strict about outbound traffic; Private deployment will need explicit allowlists and possibly proxy via their NAT. Discussed VPN vs VPC peering options.

Technical notes (SE / Solutions Eng):
- Latency sizing: for re-rank at seq_len=64, expect ~40-60ms p50 on dedicated A100-like fleet; p95 depends on batching and tail latencies - recommend initial target of 120ms p95 and monitor. For seq_len=512 completion, quantify tokens/sec and expected cost; run perf perf-shipyard tests.
- Autoscaling policy: recommend target-based autoscale with predictive scaling for scheduled promos (Black Friday). Configure burst capacity for short spikes.
- Caching approach: enable prefix/KV cache for catalog descriptions (non-personal), and per-session ephemeral cache for personalization (store in their VPC-only cache).
- Quantization: propose int8 quantization to reduce memory footprint; run quality regression tests (provided eval set).
- Embeddings: recommend batching and using Redwood Optimize suggestions for caching frequent vectors. Use FAISS in their infra for similarity; discuss vector export format and schema.

Action items / next steps (owners + tentative dates):
- Matthew: share architecture brief + Private vs Dedicated comparison doc + pricing delta by EOD 2026-03-31.
- Priya: schedule technical deep-dive with Montclair infra and security (target 2026-04-02). Create calendar invite and include SRE/Network folks from both sides.
- Luis: run tokenization diff job (sample 5k SKUs) and report mismatches (due 2026-04-01).
- Montclair (Sara): provide redacted sample prompts + typical user history shapes (examples of session contexts) and embedding batch size expectations (due 2026-04-01).
- Security: exchange KMS requirements and plan for HSM integration call (Montclair: Jenna to propose their KMS tech; Redwood: list supported KMS providers) (meeting 2026-04-06).

Open questions (need answers to finalize scope):
- Which workloads are in-scope for Private (sensitive flows only) vs Dedicated (non-sensitive re-rank)? Customer leaning to hybrid but needs Redwood recommendation on split.
- For embeddings nightly bulk, do they prefer Redwood to host ingestion pipeline or will they push vectors into their FAISS cluster?
- Can Montclair accept tokenization standardization (move SKU tokenization into a lightweight preprocessor) or do we need to ship a tokenizer compatibility layer?

Notes to self / informal:
- Emphasize we can do canary + automated rollback; good selling point for their SRE.
- Prepare sample pricing for: low-run (Dedicated 4xA100 reserved) vs Private 2-region peering. 
- Check with product on audit log retention add-on pricing (90 days export to Splunk).

Quick wins to propose on next call:
- Run a perf sandbox (1-week) with 50k sample embedding bulk and 1k QPS re-rank synthetic to prove latency/cost numbers.
- Provide tokenizer diff script and integration checklist.

Follow-up calendar invites / resources sent after call:
- Link to Private vs Dedicated brief (Confluence-1234)
- Sent initial pricing snapshot and dedicated sizing (JIRA-RET-78)
- Shared tokenization sample script (GitHub PR link above)

End notes: Montclair is very security-conscious but motivated to move quickly for checkout improvements. Prioritize KMS + VPC details on the next technical meeting. Keep docs lightweight and include concrete numbers (p95, qps, batch sizes) - they respond well to measured benchmarks.

-- Matthew
(Notes to self: convert key action items into Jira tickets after security call. Keep Priya looped in.)
